hypothesis: Query-ranked demonstrations will outperform fewshot_all's 56.7% aggregate validation accuracy at a lower injected-context cost because pooled traces show repeated answer patterns across similar inputs.

Retrieving prior mistakes as explicit wrong-answer-to-correct-answer contrasts will improve on 56.7% aggregate accuracy by helping distinguish related answer patterns and recover omitted co-occurring outputs visible in pooled errors.

Answer-pattern prototypes built from labeled inputs will retain or exceed fewshot_all's 56.7% aggregate accuracy with less than its 21,573-character average context by surfacing query-supported output patterns compactly.

On aggregate validation, full-case retrieval that tapers ubiquitous features will exceed bm25_retrieval's 46.7% accuracy by ranking substantive overlap above repeated wording, while injecting no more than 12,500 example-context characters per query.

On aggregate validation, query-matched pairs of similar cases with different verified answers will exceed contrastive_replay's 33.3% accuracy because they expose answer boundaries without anchoring on prior wrong guesses.

On aggregate validation, retrieving one high-overlap labeled excerpt per source will reach at least fewshot_all's 56.7% accuracy while keeping average injected example context below half of its 21,573-character reference.

A relevance-first selector that rewards unseen verified outputs and query-term coverage will exceed the 46.7% aggregate accuracy of BM25 retrieval while using under half of fewshot_all's 21,573-character context; this is falsified if accuracy is at most 46.7% or context reaches 10,787 characters.

Smoothed feature likelihood ratios with contrastive evidence cards will exceed the 30.0% aggregate accuracy of centroid-style label prototypes; this is falsified if aggregate accuracy is at most 30.0%.

A separate answer-audit pass informed by nearby verified corrections will exceed the 33.3% aggregate accuracy of single-pass contrastive replay; this is falsified if aggregate accuracy is at most 33.3%.

If strong full-example prompting benefits from relevance while omitting some useful answer classes, then nearest-first demonstrations with a small novelty bonus for unseen targets will exceed the 56.7% aggregate result of unfiltered full-example prompting.

If repeated identical labeled cases dilute retrieval slots, then storing one representative per normalized case and answer will improve on the 53.3% coverage-neighbor result at a similar or lower context cost.

If local answer agreement adds useful signal beyond retrieved examples, then a similarity-squared weighted answer distribution plus the closest cases will improve on example-only retrieval without relying on label-wide feature prototypes.

Across the pooled traces, removing repeated task instructions before case similarity ranking should improve retrieved-example relevance while reducing injected context; compare its accuracy and context length with coverage_neighbor_memory.

If short conduct-and-outcome excerpts retain more decisive signal per character than whole examples, this card memory should preserve accuracy with lower context than matched_excerpt_memory; compare both aggregate accuracy and context length.

If multi-label examples in the pooled traces are driving answer omissions, checking a provisional answer against retrieved evidence should improve aggregate accuracy over one-pass fewshot_all; compare accuracy and context length.

Separating event facts from conclusion and procedural material will improve aggregate accuracy over broad neighbor retrieval while using less context, because close factual analogies will be easier to compare.
Selecting demonstrations for diversity of joint answer bundles will improve aggregate accuracy over label-diverse demonstrations, especially when a correct output has multiple components.

A frequency-ranked inventory of answer components from nearby verified examples will improve aggregate accuracy over a second-pass answer check by prompting completeness checks without discarding case-level evidence.
